flawed_step: The claim incorrectly assumes that a degree sequence determines a graph up to isomorphism.
counterexample: Let G have vertex set {1,2,3,4,5,6} and edges {12,23,34,45,56,61}, so G is the 6-cycle C6. Let H have the same vertex set and edges {12,23,31,45,56,64}, so H is the disjoint union of two triangles. Both are finite simple graphs with degree sequence {2,2,2,2,2,2}. They are not isomorphic because G is connected while H is disconnected.
assessment_summary: Two graphs can have the same number of vertices and identical degree multisets without being isomorphic; C6 and two disjoint triangles give a concrete counterexample.
